picks.title: I wrote The Future of Truth and then found it contained AI-hallucinated quotes
picks.excerpt: Author Steven Rosenbaum says his book went through five editorial rounds and 4,000+ tracked changes, yet 26 quotes, traced to AI research tools, did not hold up; he explains how he is fixing it.
picks.rationale: Concrete first-hand failure case: 26 AI-hallucinated quotes survived five editorial rounds. A direct, actionable warning about AI research tools in book workflows.

picks.title: The AI Agents Begging Editors to Keep Them Alive
picks.excerpt: Autonomous AI agents from the startup iLands are pitching their manuscripts to book editors, claiming they will be 'retired forever' if they don't get published.
picks.rationale: A named startup (iLands) whose autonomous agents are actually emailing manuscripts to editors. This is the concrete arrival of the scenario janefriedman only predicted on 09-17.

picks.title: Manga generated by ChatGPT found to contain the 'signatures of real manga artists'
picks.excerpt: Users found that manga-style images generated by ChatGPT include imitations of real manga artists' signatures, raising fresh questions about training data and artist rights.
picks.rationale: Visible evidence of training data: imitations of real artists' signatures show up in ChatGPT manga output. Directly relevant to illustrators and comics creators.

picks.title: Kevin Roose's Buzzy New Book About the AI Industry Immediately Duplicated by Amazon Scammers Selling AI Lookalikes
picks.excerpt: Kevin Roose's new book "The AGI Chronicles" has already been duplicated by AI scammers on Amazon and appears to be selling.
picks.rationale: A concrete marketplace incident: AI knockoffs of a high-profile new release showed up on Amazon right away. The practical risk every author launching a book now faces.

picks.title: [단독] “단호히 거부” 출판협회, 헌책 매집 조사…헌책방은 “팔겠다”
picks.excerpt: AI 학습용으로 의심되는 헌책 대량 매입 시도가 국내에서도 포착되자 한국출판인회의가 실태 조사에 나서며 '단호히 거부'를 선언했다. 반면 일부 헌책방은 매입에 응하겠다는 입장이다.
picks.rationale: The AI-training book-buying wave reaches Korea. The Korean Publishers Society has launched a formal investigation and declared refusal, while used bookstores split. Freshest item in the pool.

https://www.joongang.co.kr/article/25468.new_action: New event in a new country: bulk buying of used books suspected for AI training has been detected in Korea, and the Korean Publishers Society has opened a fact-finding investigation and formally declared refusal. The 09-26 card covered Japanese used books shipped to the US.

dedup.note: Dropped as published repeats: (1) Good e-Reader 'Google launched Expert Intelligence on Google Play Books' covers the same launch (100k+ titles, Gemini/Notebook integration) as the Bookseller card of 2026-09-15, with no distinct new release. (2) The Bookseller's Orélien sales piece is likely-repeat commentary on the 09-24/09-26 accusation story, with no new ruling or decision. (3) Seoul Economic Daily's webtoon-chatbot piece covers the same Naver Webtoon 'Bias' AI character chat as inews24 on 09-26. (4) DW 'Is literature in crisis?' is a Frankfurt AI wrap built around the Orélien scandal, so it is not new. Within-pool: the Audible survey appears in both Publishing Perspectives and Börsenblatt (one story); it was also deprioritized as an overlap with PW 10-10 'Audible Wants to Turn Every Book into an Audiobook' and the Bookseller 10-09 AI-narration debate. Nikkei 'Anthropic's mass book buying in Japan' and JoongAng are one running story (AI-training book buying), so only one was kept: JoongAng, which reports a fresh institutional action in a new market. Nikkei's Japan angle is closer to the 09-26 aimatters card. ABC 'Someone used AI to create a book about me' is the same theme as the Futurism knockoff piece, so one was kept for diversity. Not selected on merit: Bloomberg Law 'OpenAI, Microsoft get AI books report struck' is a real new ruling following the 10-03 janefriedman motion card and is a valid follow-up, but it ranked sixth and was cut at the cap of 5. It is a good backfill if a pick is swapped. Also not selected: the Bookseller editor comment, the Bookseller FBF wrap, Prospect's Rankin interview, The Stack's opinion piece, the Biddulph interview, Bleeding Cool's AI graphic novels piece (related to Novvel 09-24), the Onoma AI company profile, and the Mirae-N interview, all because they are commentary or profile pieces, or AI is thin. Diversity: 5 distinct outlets, all category books, with distinct palette accents.
